data.jobspec:
#!/bin/sh

#flux: -n 64
#flux: --tasks-per-node=8
#flux: -o flux.%J

# Omitted Slurm option --partition=t1standard. In Flux, queue selection is typically handled by the broker configuration.
# This might have performance implications if the partition selected for specific hardware.

# Omitted Slurm option --mail-user. Flux does not have a direct equivalent for email notifications in jobspec.

cd $FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR

# Generate a list of allocated nodes; will serve as a machinefile for mpirun
flux exec -r all hostname | sort -n > ./nodes.$FLUX_JOB_ID

make streams

# Clean up the machinefile
rm ./nodes.$FLUX_JOB_ID

issues: The script allocates 64 parallel tasks but does not use a parallel launcher (e.g., 'mpirun', 'flux mini run') to execute the 'make streams' command. The command will run as a single task on one node.

issues: The script requests 64 parallel tasks (-n 64) but executes 'make streams' as a single serial command. To utilize the allocated resources, a parallel launcher like 'flux mini run -n 64' or 'mpirun' is required.
The script generates a node list file ('nodes.$FLUX_JOB_ID') but never uses it, and then deletes it. This is unnecessary work if the intent was to use a Flux-native launcher like 'flux mini run'.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/sh

#SBATCH --partition=t1standard
#SBATCH --ntasks=64
#SBATCH --tasks-per-node=8
#SBATCH --mail-user=elbueler@alaska.edu
#SBATCH --output=slurm.%j

cd $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR

# Generate a list of allocated nodes; will serve as a machinefile for mpirun
srun -l /bin/hostname | sort -n | awk '{print $2}' > ./nodes.$SLURM_JOB_ID

make streams

# Clean up the machinefile
rm ./nodes.$SLURM_JOB_ID
